title: Clinic Dash
premise: A cute mascot-like runner dashes through a glowing futuristic clinic corridor, collecting bandages for Poppy while avoiding animal-shaped hazards.
interaction_model: Single-button endless runner with auto-forward motion and jump timing via tap, click, Space, or Arrow Up.
objective: Survive as long as possible and collect as many bandages as possible before colliding with a hazard.
progression: Runs begin immediately after start, difficulty ramps through increasing scroll speed, score rises through bandage pickups, and failure restarts the run loop.
theme: Whimsical medical rescue framed inside a neon sci-fi hospital hallway.
mood: Playful, energetic, arcade-like, cute, and slightly surreal.
confidence_notes: High confidence in the endless-runner structure because the full gameplay loop, scoring, collisions, and controls are explicit in code.
Moderate confidence in the narrative framing: the title, bandages, and Poppy references imply a care/rescue theme, but the character role is not fully spelled out.
High confidence that score-based replayability, not level completion, is the intended progression.
recreation_prompt: Create a polished single-screen endless runner called 'Clinic Dash' where a cute pink mascot-like patient or helper automatically runs through a glowing futuristic hospital corridor and the player uses one-button jumping controls to survive. The only direct input should be jump, triggered by tap, click, Space, or Arrow Up, while forward motion is automatic and the world scrolls from right to left. Populate the run with mixed hazards at different heights and sizes—such as ants, bears, leopards, eagles, and bats—that instantly end the run on contact, plus collectible bandages that increase score when touched. Use simple gravity-based jump physics with grounded landing, and raise the difficulty over time by gradually increasing scroll speed so reaction windows become tighter. Present the game with a full-screen canvas, a neon blue sci-fi clinic background, a glossy start panel, a compact score HUD, and a game-over overlay that shows the final bandage count and a restart button. Add juicy feedback such as upbeat background music, jump/land/pickup/fail sound effects, floating text callouts when a bandage is collected, and small animated reaction panels for success and failure. Keep the structure replayable and arcade-focused, with no level ending—just survive longer, collect more bandages for Poppy, and chase a higher score.
